analysis: seed-level percentile bootstrap for the strict-freeze arm comparisons of Paper A, with paired bootstrap for the arm differences

method.resampling_unit: seed (run), independent within each arm; arm differences resample seed pairs
method.statistic: arithmetic mean of the per-seed arm value
method.dispersion: sd with ddof=1 (sample) and ddof=0 (population) both reported; the convention the manuscript's printed spread matches is recorded per table under sd_convention
method.note: with 3-5 seeds per arm a percentile CI is coarse by construction; it bounds how much of an arm separation can be attributed to seed noise and should not be read as a 5%% false-positive guarantee

scope_note: Paper A (`paper合/`) is the strict-freeze arm comparison of Tables tab:position_strict, tab:vlm and tab:llava. The +1478/+5048 examples in the commissioning brief belong to Paper 3 and are reproduced in the labelled addendum below.

cross_paper_addendum_p3_allocation.why_present: The commissioning brief cites +1478 +/- 1563 and +5048 +/- 1900 as Paper A strict-freeze arm comparisons. They are not in paper合/: they are the Gamma-guided vs uniform allocation arms of Paper 3 (paper3/paper_ieee/sections/experiments.tex, 'Counterfactual validation'). Reproduced here under an explicit addendum so the digits travel with their real provenance.

capacity_matched.paired_versus_unpaired_note: the manuscript quotes the unpaired Welch test (p = 0.0055, df = 9.64). Because the two arms were run at the same six seeds, the seed pairs can be kept; the paired bootstrap below then resolves the same contrast far more sharply (no resample of the paired differences reaches zero). The two statements are not in conflict: they differ in whether the between-seed variance is removed.

matched_training_loss.power_note: two seeds per arm as archived; the CI covers the seed spread only

random_allocation.gamma_percentile_definition: percent of the 30 individual random runs below the Gamma-guided mean (archived definition, tools/_p458_random_pool_test.py lines 204-207)
random_allocation.paired_bootstrap_note: the gamma arm is one plan, so the paired form here reduces to a one-sample bootstrap of the pool mean minus the fixed gamma mean; it is reported for completeness only
